If you lend money to a poor person among my people who lives among you, do not act toward him as a creditor, and do not take interest from him.
If you take your neighbor’s garment as a pledge, return it to him by sunset.
For it is his only garment, the covering for his body. What will he sleep in? If he prays to me, I will hear him, for I am merciful.
You must not revile a judge or curse a leader of your people.
You must not delay offering the first produce of your threshing floor and the first yield of your presses. You must give me the firstborn of your sons.
Do the same with your cattle and your flocks. The young animal must remain with its mother for seven days; on the eighth day you must give it to me.
You must be holy people to me. Do not eat flesh torn by a wild animal; throw it to the dogs.
You must not accept a false report. You must not join hands with a guilty person to be a false witness for him.
Do not follow the majority in doing wrong. Do not give testimony in a lawsuit that bends justice by following the majority who turn it aside.
You must not favor a poor person in his lawsuit.
When you come across your enemy’s ox or donkey wandering astray, you must return it to him.
If you see your enemy's donkey lying under its load, and you want to refrain from helping him lift it, you must nevertheless help him lift it.
You must not deny a poor person justice in his lawsuit.
Keep far away from a false accusation. Do not kill the innocent or the righteous, for I will not acquit the guilty.
Do not accept a bribe, for a bribe blinds the eyes of those who are wise in judgment and distorts the words of the innocent.
Do not oppress foreigners living among you. You yourselves know how foreigners feel, because you were foreigners in the land of Egypt.
For six years you shall sow your land and gather its produce.

In the seventh year, leave it fallow and let it rest, so that the poor among your people may eat. The wild animals may eat what they leave behind. Do the same with your vineyards and your olive trees.
Do your work for six days, but rest on the seventh day, so that your ox and your donkey may rest, and the son of your female slave and the foreigner living in your villages may be refreshed.
Be careful to observe everything I have told you. Do not mention the names of other gods, and do not let them enter your thoughts.
Three times a year you shall celebrate a festival for me.

Observe the Festival of Unleavened Bread. Eat unleavened bread for seven days, as I commanded you, in the month of blossoms, because in the month of blossoms you came out of Egypt. Do not appear before me empty-handed.
Also observe the Festival of Harvest, with the first of the grain you sow in the field, and the Festival of Ingathering at the end of the year, when you gather your produce from the field.
Three times a year all your males shall appear before the Lord your God.
Do not offer the blood of a sacrifice with leavened bread, and do not let the fat of the festival offering remain overnight until morning.
You shall bring the first produce of your land to the house of the Lord your God. Do not cook a young goat in its mother's milk.
Look, I am sending an angel ahead of you to guard you on the way and to bring you into the land I have prepared.
Be on your guard before him and obey his voice. Do not oppose him, lest he refuse to forgive your sins, because my name is upon him.
If you faithfully obey his voice and do everything he tells you, I will hate those who hate you and afflict your enemies.
For my angel will go before you and bring you to the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Canaanites, Hivites, and Jebusites, and I will destroy them.
Do not bow down to their gods or serve them, and do not imitate their deeds. Instead, completely overthrow them and smash their sacred pillars to pieces.
You shall serve the Lord your God, and he will bless your bread and your water and remove afflictions from your homes.
No one in your land will miscarry or be barren, and I will give you the full number of your days.
I will send terror of me ahead of you and destroy all the peoples you go against. I will make your enemies turn their backs before you.
I will send hornets ahead of you and destroy the Canaanites and the Hittites before you.
I will not destroy them before you in a single year, so that the land does not become desolate and wild animals multiply against you.
Little by little I will destroy them before you, until you grow strong and take possession of the land.

I will establish your boundary from the Red Sea to the sea of the Philistines, and from the wilderness to the River. For I am handing the inhabitants of the land over to you, and you shall destroy them.
Do not make a covenant with them or with their gods.
They shall not live in your land, lest they cause you to sin against me. Do not serve their gods, so that they do not become a snare to you.
He said to Moses, “Come up to the Lord, you and Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, and seventy men from the elders of Israel, and bow down from a distance.”
“Moses alone is to approach the Lord. The others must not approach, and the people must not come up with him.”
Moses came and told the people all the words of the Lord and all the judgments. All the people cried out with one voice and said, “We will do everything the Lord has said.”
Moses wrote down all the words of the Lord. He rose early in the morning and built an altar at the foot of the mountain, and twelve pillars for the twelve tribes of Israel.
He sent young men from among the Israelites, and they offered whole burnt offerings and sacrificed bulls as peace offerings to the Lord.
Moses took half the blood and put it in a basin, and poured the other half of the blood on the altar.
He took the book of the covenant and read it before the people. They said, “We will obey and do everything the Lord has said.”
Moses took the blood and sprinkled it on the people, saying, “This is the blood of the covenant that the Lord has made with you in accordance with all these words.”
Moses and Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel went up.
They saw the God of Israel. Beneath his feet was something like paving made of sapphire bricks, as clear as the vault of heaven.
He did not lay his hand on the elders of the Israelites. They saw God, and they ate and drank.
The Lord said to Moses, “Come up to me on the mountain and remain there. I will give you stone tablets, and the laws and commandments that I have written to teach them.”
Moses rose with Hoshea, his assistant, and Moses went up the mountain of God.
He said to the elders, “Wait here for us until we return to you. Aaron and Hur are here with you. Whoever has a dispute should come before them.”
Moses went up the mountain, and the cloud covered it.
The glory of the Lord rested on Mount Sinai, and the cloud covered it for six days. On the seventh day the Lord called to Moses from within the cloud.
The appearance of the Lord’s glory was like a burning fire on the summit of the mountain in the sight of all the house of Israel.
Moses entered the cloud and went up the mountain. Moses remained on the mountain for forty days and forty nights.
The Lord spoke with Moses and said to him:
Tell the house of Israel to set aside an offering for me. You shall receive the offering from everyone whose heart prompts him to give.
This is the offering you shall receive from them: gold, silver, and bronze.
“And blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, fine linen, and goats’ hair;”
“And rams’ skins dyed red, blue skins, and boxwood;”
“And oil for lighting, spices for the anointing oil and for the fragrant incense;”
“And beryl stones and precious stones for the ephod and the breastpiece.”
“They are to make me a sanctuary, and I will dwell among them.”
“They are to make everything just as I show you—the pattern of the tabernacle and of all its furnishings.”
They shall make an ark of boxwood, two and a half cubits long, a cubit and a half wide, and a cubit and a half high.
Overlay it with pure gold. You shall overlay it outside and inside, and make a gold molding around it.
Forge four gold rings for it and place them at its four corners: two rings on one side and two rings on its other side.
Make poles of boxwood and overlay them with gold.
Insert the poles into the rings on the sides of the ark, so that the ark may be carried with them.
The poles shall remain in the rings of the ark and shall not be removed from them.
Place in the ark the testimony that I will give you.
Make an atonement cover of pure gold, two and a half cubits long and one and a half cubits wide.
Make two cherubim of gold. Make them as cast work at the two ends of the atonement cover.
Make one cherub at this end and another cherub at the other end of the atonement cover. Make the two cherubim at its two ends.
The cherubim are to spread their wings upward, covering the atonement cover with their wings. Their faces are to face one another; the faces of the cherubim are to be above the atonement cover.
Place the atonement cover on top of the ark, and place in the ark the testimony that I will give you.
I will meet with you there and speak with you from above the atonement cover, from between the two cherubim above the ark of the testimony, about everything I command you concerning the Israelites.
Make a table of boxwood, two cubits long, one cubit wide, and one and a half cubits high.
Overlay it with pure gold and make a gold molding around it.
Make a rim around it, a handbreadth high, and make a gold molding around its rim.
Make four gold rings for it. Make the four gold rings at its four corners, above its four legs.
Its rings shall be opposite its rim, as holders for the poles used to carry the table.
Make poles of boxwood and overlay them with gold, so that the table can be carried with them.
Make its dishes, spoons, pitchers, and bowls used for pouring. Make them of pure gold.
Place the bread of the Presence on the table before me continually.
Make a lampstand of pure gold. Make the lampstand of cast work. Its base, branches, cups, apple-shaped knobs, and lilies are to be part of it.
Six branches are to extend from its sides: three branches from one side of the lampstand and three branches from its other side.

Three cups are to be set on one branch, with apple-shaped knobs and lilies, and three cups are to be set on another branch, with apple-shaped knobs and lilies. It is to be this way on all six branches extending from the lampstand.
On the lampstand there shall be four cups, with apple-shaped ornaments and lilies.

There is to be an apple-shaped knob beneath two branches extending from it, an apple-shaped knob beneath two branches extending from it, and an apple-shaped knob beneath two branches extending from it. It is to be this way for the six branches extending from the lampstand.
Its apple-shaped ornaments and its branches shall be part of it. The whole of it shall be a single casting of pure gold.
Make its seven lamps, and light its lamps so that they shine in front of it.
Make its tongs and its snuff dishes of pure gold.
Make it and all these utensils from a talent of pure gold.
See that you make them according to the pattern that I am showing you on the mountain.
Make the tabernacle with ten curtains of twisted fine linen, blue, purple, and scarlet yarn. Make them with cherubim, the work of a skilled craftsman.
Each curtain is to be twenty-eight cubits long and four cubits wide. All the curtains are to have the same measurements.
Five curtains are to be joined to one another, and five curtains are to be joined to one another.
Make blue loops along the edge of the curtain at the end of one joined set. Do the same along the edge of the curtain at the end of the other joined set.
Make fifty loops along the edge of one curtain, and make fifty loops along the edge of the curtain in the other joined set. The loops are to line up opposite one another.
Make fifty gold clasps and join the curtains to one another with the clasps, so that the tabernacle will be one unit.
Make curtains of hair as a covering for the tabernacle. Make eleven curtains.
Each of these curtains is to be thirty cubits long and four cubits wide. All eleven curtains are to have the same measurements.
Join five curtains together and six curtains together. Fold the sixth curtain double at the front of the tabernacle.
Make fifty loops along the edge of the curtain at the end of one joined set, and fifty loops along the edge of the curtain in the other joined set.
Make fifty bronze clasps and put the clasps into the loops. Join the tabernacle together so that it will be one unit.
As for the excess left over from the curtains of the tabernacle, let the remaining half-curtain hang over the back of the tabernacle.
The cubit on one side and the cubit on the other side that remain along the length of the tabernacle curtains are to hang over the sides of the tabernacle, on this side and that side, to cover it.
Make a covering for the tabernacle from rams’ skins dyed red, with rams’ skins dyed blue above them.
Make upright boards of boxwood for the tabernacle.
Each board is to be ten cubits long and a cubit and a half wide.
Each board is to have two tenons, aligned opposite one another. Make all the boards of the tabernacle this way.
Make twenty boards for the south side of the tabernacle.
Make forty silver bases beneath the twenty boards: two bases beneath one board for its two tenons, and two bases beneath another board for its two tenons.
For the other side of the tabernacle, on the north, make twenty boards.
And forty silver bases: two bases beneath one board and two bases beneath another board.
For the rear of the tabernacle, on the west, make six boards.
Make two boards for the corner of the tabernacle at the rear.
They are to be level at the bottom and joined together at the top at a single ring. Both supports at the two corners are to be made this way.
There are to be eight boards, with sixteen silver bases: two bases beneath one board and two bases beneath another board.
Make bars of boxwood, five for the boards on one side of the tabernacle,
And five crossbars for the boards on the other side of the tabernacle, and five crossbars for the boards on the other side, at the rear of the tabernacle, to the west.
Pass the middle bar through the middle of the boards, from one end to the other.
Overlay the boards with gold, and make gold rings as holders for the crossbars. Overlay the crossbars with gold.
Set up the tabernacle in its prescribed form, as I showed you on the mountain.
Make a curtain of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and finely spun linen. Make it with cherubim, the work of a skilled craftsman.
Hang it on four pillars of boxwood overlaid with gold, with gold capitals, standing on four silver bases.
Place the curtain beneath the boards, and bring the ark of the testimony in there, behind the curtain. The curtain will separate the Holy Place from the Most Holy Place for you.
Place the atonement cover on the ark of the testimony in the Most Holy Place.
Place the table outside the curtain, and the lampstand opposite the table on the south side of the tabernacle. Place the table on the north side.
Make a curtain for the entrance of the tabernacle, of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and finely spun linen, the work of an embroiderer.
Make five boxwood pillars for the curtain and overlay them with gold. Their capitals are to be gold. Make five bronze bases for them.
Make an altar of boxwood, five cubits long and five cubits wide. The altar is to be square and three cubits high.
Make its horns on its four corners. Its horns shall be of one piece with it. Overlay it with bronze.
Make its pots for its service, its shovels, its basins, its forks, and its firepans. Make all its utensils of bronze.
Make a bronze grating in the form of a net, and make four bronze rings on the four sides of the grating.
Place it beneath the lower ledge of the altar, so that the grating reaches halfway up the altar.
Make poles for the altar, poles of boxwood, and overlay them with bronze.
Insert the poles into the rings. They shall be on the two sides of the altar when it is carried.
Make it hollow, out of boards. They shall make it just as I showed you on the mountain.
Make a courtyard for the tabernacle. On the south side, the courtyard hangings are to be of finely spun linen, one stretch of hangings a hundred cubits long.
Its twenty pillars and their twenty bases are to be bronze. The capitals of the pillars and their overlay are to be silver.
Likewise, on the north side, there are to be hangings a hundred cubits long, with twenty pillars and their twenty bronze bases. The capitals of the pillars and their overlay are to be silver.
Across the width of the courtyard on the west side, there are to be hangings fifty cubits long, with ten pillars and their ten bases.
The width of the courtyard on the east side shall be fifty cubits.
The hangings on one side shall be fifteen cubits, with three pillars and three bases.
On the other side there shall be fifteen hangings, with three pillars and three bases.

For the entrance of the courtyard, there is to be a curtain twenty cubits long, of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and finely spun linen, the work of an embroiderer, with four pillars and their four bases.
All the pillars around the courtyard are to be overlaid with silver. Their capitals are to be silver and their bases bronze.
The courtyard is to be a hundred cubits long, fifty by fifty in width, and five cubits high, with hangings of finely spun linen and bronze bases.
All the utensils of the tabernacle for all its service, all its pegs, and all the pegs of the courtyard are to be bronze.
You must command the Israelites to bring you pure, pressed olive oil to keep the lamps burning continually.

In the tent of meeting, outside the curtain that is over the testimony, Aaron and his sons must tend them from evening until morning before the Lord. This is a lasting ordinance for the Israelites throughout your generations.
Bring your brother Aaron and his sons with him near to you from among the Israelites to serve me as priests: Aaron, and Aaron’s sons Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
Make holy garments for your brother Aaron, for honor and glory.
Speak to all those skilled in heart whom I have filled with a spirit of wisdom. They must make sacred garments for Aaron, to consecrate him to serve me as a priest.

These are the garments they must make for them: an apron, an ephod, a breastpiece, a linen tunic, a turban, and a sash. They must make sacred garments for your brother Aaron and his sons to serve me as priests.
They shall take gold, blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and fine linen.
They must make the ephod of gold, blue and purple material, scarlet yarn, and spun fine linen, the work of a skilled craftsman.
It shall have two shoulder pieces attached at its two sides, so that it is joined together.
The sash of the ephod that is on it must be of one piece with it and made in the same way: of gold, blue and purple material, scarlet yarn, and spun fine linen.
Take two beryl stones and engrave on them the names of the sons of Israel.
Engrave six of their names on one stone, and engrave the six remaining names on the other stone, in their birth order.
Engrave the two stones with the names of the sons of Israel, as a skilled craftsman engraves stones with the engravings of a seal. Make them secured and set in gold.
Place the two stones on the shoulder pieces of the ephod as memorial stones for the Israelites. Aaron must carry their names before the Lord on his two shoulders as a memorial.
Make gold settings.
Make two doubled chains of pure gold, braided work, and attach the two doubled chains to the settings.
Make a breastpiece of judgment, the work of a skilled craftsman. Make it in the same way as the ephod; make it of gold, blue and purple material, scarlet yarn, and spun fine linen.
It shall be square when folded double, a span long and a span wide.
Fill it with a full setting of stones, four rows of stones. The first row is a ruby, a topaz, and an emerald: one row.
The next row shall be a garnet, a sapphire, and a diamond.
The third row shall be a jacinth, a carbuncle, and a calf’s-eye stone.
The fourth row is a chrysolite, a beryl, and a jasper. They must be secured and set in gold in their settings.
The stones must correspond to the names of the sons of Israel, twelve according to their names. They must be engraved with the engravings of a seal, each with its own name, for the twelve tribes.
Make paired chains for the breastpiece, braided work of pure gold.
Make two rings of pure gold for the breastpiece, and put the two rings on the two sides of the breastpiece.
Attach the two gold braids to the two rings on the two sides of the breastpiece.
Attach the two braids to the two settings, and attach them to the shoulder pieces of the ephod at its front.
Make two gold rings and put them on the two sides of the breastpiece, on its inner edge facing the ephod.
Make two gold rings and put them on the two shoulder pieces of the ephod, below, at its front, close to its joining, above the sash of the ephod.
They must fasten the breastpiece by its loops to the loops of the ephod with a blue cord, so that it rests above the sash of the ephod and the breastpiece does not come away from the ephod.
Aaron must carry the names of the sons of Israel in the breastpiece of judgment over his chest when he enters the sanctuary, as a continual memorial before the Lord.

Place the Urim and Thummim on the breastpiece of judgment. They must be over his chest when he enters before the Lord. Aaron must continually carry the judgments of the Israelites over his chest before the Lord.
Make the robe of the ephod entirely of blue yarn.
Its opening for the head must be in its center. There must be a woven border all around its opening, like the opening of a coat of mail, so that it does not tear.
Make pomegranates of blue and purple material and scarlet yarn all around its hem, with gold bells between them all around.
There shall be gold bells, one by one, and pomegranates all around the hem of the robe.
It shall be on Aaron when he serves, and its sound shall be heard when he enters the sanctuary before the Lord and when he comes out, so that he will not die.
Make a crown of pure gold, and engrave on it, like the engraving of a seal: “Holy to the Lord.”
Attach it to a blue cord. It shall be on the turban, at the front of the turban.

It shall be on Aaron’s forehead. Aaron shall bear the guilt connected with the holy things that the Israelites consecrate as all their holy gifts. It shall always be on his forehead, so that they may be accepted before the Lord.
Make a tunic of fine linen, and make a turban of fine linen. Make a sash with embroidered work.
Make tunics for Aaron’s sons, and make sashes for them. Make caps for them, for honor and glory.
Clothe your brother Aaron and his sons with him in these garments. Anoint them, ordain them, and consecrate them to serve me as priests.
Make linen undergarments for them to cover their naked flesh. They shall reach from their waists to their thighs.

Aaron and his sons shall wear them when they enter the tent of meeting and when they approach the altar to serve in the sanctuary, so that they do not incur guilt and die. This is a lasting statute for him and his descendants after him.
This is what you shall do for them to consecrate them to serve me as priests: take one young bull and two rams without blemish.
And unleavened bread, unleavened [?] mixed with oil, and unleavened wafers mixed with oil. Make them from fine wheat flour.
Put them in one basket and bring them in the basket, together with the bull and the two rams.
Bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance of the tent of meeting, and wash them with water.
Take the garments and clothe Aaron in the tunic, the undergarment, the turban, the ephod, and the breastpiece. Fasten it on him with the sash of the ephod.
Put the turban on his head, and put the holy crown on the turban.
Take the anointing oil, pour it on his head, and anoint him.
Bring his sons forward and clothe them in tunics.
Tie sashes around Aaron and his sons, and put caps on them. Their priesthood shall belong to them by a lasting statute. You shall ordain Aaron and his sons.
Bring the bull before the tent of meeting. Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands on the bull’s head.
Slaughter the bull before the Lord at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
Take some of the bull’s blood and sprinkle it on the horns of the altar with your finger. Pour out all the blood at the base of the altar.
Take all the fat covering the entrails, the lobe of the liver, and the two kidneys with their fat, and offer them up on the altar.
Burn the bull’s flesh, its hide, and its dung in the fire outside the camp. It is a sin offering.
Take one ram, and Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands on the ram’s head.
Slaughter the ram, take some of its blood, and sprinkle it all around the altar.
Cut the ram into pieces, wash its entrails and legs, and put them with its pieces and its head.
Offer up the whole ram on the altar. It is a burnt offering to the Lord, a pleasing aroma, an offering to the Lord.
Take the second ram, and Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands on the ram’s head.

Slaughter the ram and take some of its blood. Sprinkle it on Aaron’s right earlobe, on his sons’ right earlobes, on the thumbs of their right hands, and on the big toes of their right feet. Sprinkle the blood all around the altar.

Take some of the blood on the altar and some of the anointing oil, and sprinkle them on Aaron and his garments, and on his sons and their garments with him. He and his garments, and his sons and their garments with him, shall be consecrated.
Take from the ram the fat, the fat tail, the fat covering the entrails, the lobe of the liver, the two kidneys and the fat on them, and the right thigh, because it is a ram of ordination.
And one loaf of bread, one loaf of bread made with oil, and one wafer from the basket of unleavened bread that is before the Lord.
Place them all in Aaron’s hands and in his sons’ hands, and set them apart as an offering before the Lord.
Take them from their hands, and offer up the breast from the ram on the altar as a burnt offering, for a pleasing aroma before the Lord. It is an offering to the Lord.
Take the breast from Aaron’s ram of ordination and set it apart as an offering before the Lord. It shall be your portion.
Consecrate the breast that is set apart and the thigh that is set apart, which were set apart and lifted up from the ram of ordination belonging to Aaron and his sons.

This shall belong to Aaron and his sons as a lasting due from the Israelites, because it is an offering set apart. It shall be an offering set apart by the Israelites from their sacrifices of well-being, an offering set apart for the Lord.
Aaron’s holy garments shall belong to his sons after him, so that they may be anointed and ordained in them.
The priest from among his sons who succeeds him and enters the tent of meeting to serve in the sanctuary shall wear them for seven days.
Take the ram of ordination and boil its meat in a holy place.
Aaron and his sons shall eat the meat of the ram and the bread in the basket at the entrance to the tent of meeting.
They shall eat the things through which atonement is made for them, to ordain and consecrate them. No outsider shall eat them, because they are holy.
If any of the meat of the ordination offering or any of the bread remains until morning, burn what remains in the fire. It must not be eaten, because these things are holy.
Do for Aaron and his sons just as I commanded you. Ordain them over seven days.
Each day offer a bull as a sin offering for atonement. Sprinkle the altar when you make atonement for it, and anoint it to make it holy.
For seven days make atonement for the altar and consecrate it. The altar will be most holy, and whoever approaches the altar will become holy.
This is what you shall offer on the altar: two year-old lambs each day, regularly.
Offer one lamb in the morning, and offer the other lamb in the evening.
Also offer a tenth of a measure of fine flour mixed with a quarter of a hin of pressed oil, and a drink offering of a quarter of a hin of wine for the one lamb.
Offer the second lamb in the evening. Offer it with the same grain offering and drink offering as in the morning, as a pleasing aroma, an offering to the Lord.
This is to be a regular burnt offering throughout your generations at the entrance to the tent of meeting before the Lord, where I will meet with you to speak with you.
There I will meet with the Israelites, and I will be sanctified in my glory.
I will consecrate the tent of meeting and the altar. I will also consecrate Aaron and his sons to serve me as priests.
I will dwell among the Israelites and be their God.
They will know that I am the Lord their God, who brought them out of the land of Egypt, and I will dwell among them. I am the Lord their God.
Make an altar for burning incense. Make it from boxwood.
Its length is to be one cubit and its width one cubit. It is to be square and two cubits high. Its horns are to be of one piece with it.
Overlay it with pure gold—its top, its sides all around, and its horns. Make a gold molding around it.
Make two gold rings for it below its molding. Make them at its two corners, on its two sides. They will serve as holders for the poles used to carry it.
Make the poles from boxwood and overlay them with gold.
Place it in front of the curtain that is before the ark of the testimony, in front of the atonement cover that is over the testimony. I will meet with you there.
Aaron is to burn fragrant incense on it every morning. He is to burn it when he tends the lamps.
When Aaron lights the lamps at twilight, he is to burn incense on it. There is to be incense regularly before the Lord throughout your generations.
You shall not offer unauthorized incense on it, or a burnt offering or a grain offering, and you shall not pour a drink offering on it.

Once a year Aaron is to make atonement on the horns of the altar with the blood of the sin offering for atonement. Once a year he is to make atonement for it throughout your generations. It is most holy to the Lord.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
When you take a census of the Israelites to count them, each man is to give the Lord a ransom for his life when you count them, so that no plague of death will come among them when you count them.
This is what everyone who is counted must give: half a shekel according to the sanctuary weights. A shekel is twenty zuzim. Half a shekel is the contribution to the Lord.
Everyone included in the count, from twenty years old and upward, shall give the contribution to the Lord.
The rich must not give more, and the poor must not give less than half a shekel when giving the contribution to the Lord to make atonement for your lives.
Take the atonement money from the Israelites and give it for the service of the tent of meeting. It will be a memorial for the Israelites before the Lord, to make atonement for their lives.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
Make a bronze basin with a bronze stand for washing. Place it between the tent of meeting and the altar, and put water in it.
Aaron and his sons shall wash their hands and feet with water from it.
When they enter the tent of meeting, they are to wash with water so that they do not die, and when they approach the altar to minister and to burn an offering to the Lord.
They are to wash their hands and feet so that they do not die. This will be a lasting ordinance for them, for him and his descendants throughout their generations.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
Take for yourself the finest spices: five hundred of pure myrrh, half as much fragrant cinnamon—two hundred and fifty—and two hundred and fifty of fragrant cane.
And five hundred shekels of cassia according to the sanctuary standard, and a hin of olive oil.
Make it into a holy anointing oil, a fragrant blend prepared by a perfumer. It is to be an oil for anointing and consecration.
With it you shall anoint the tent of meeting and the ark of the testimony,
the table and all its utensils, the lampstand and its utensils, and the incense altar,
the altar of burnt offering and all its utensils, and the basin and its stand.
Consecrate them, and they shall be most holy. Whatever touches them shall become holy.
You shall anoint Aaron and his sons and consecrate them to serve me as priests.
Speak to the house of Israel and say: This is to be my anointing oil for consecration throughout your generations.
It must not be rubbed on human flesh, and you must not make anything like it, because it is holy and must be holy to you.
Anyone who compounds anything like it or gives any of it to an outsider shall be cut off from his people.
The Lord said to Moses, “Take aromatic spices: stacte, onycha, and galbanum—spices together with pure frankincense. They must be in equal weights.”
Make it into fragrant incense, the work of a perfumer, blended and pure, for holy use.
Grind some of it into a fine powder, and put some before the testimony in the tent of meeting, where I will meet with you. There it must be most holy to you.
As for the incense you make, you shall not make any like it for yourselves. You shall regard it as holy to the Lord.
Anyone who makes anything like it to enjoy its fragrance shall be cut off from his people.”
The Lord spoke with Moses and said to him,
“See, I have called by name Bezalel son of Uri, son of Hur, from the tribe of Judah.
I have filled him with the Spirit of God, with wisdom, understanding, knowledge, and every kind of craftsmanship,
to teach craftsmanship, to work in gold, silver, and bronze,
and in the craft of finishing stones and in woodworking, to do every kind of work.

And look, I have appointed Oholiab son of Ahisamach, from the tribe of Dan, to be with him. I have put wisdom into the hearts of all who are skilled, so that they may make everything I have commanded you.
the tent of meeting, the ark of the testimony, the atonement cover upon it, and all the furnishings of the tabernacle;
the table and all its utensils, the pure lampstand and all its utensils, and the altar of incense;
the altar of burnt offering and all its utensils, and the basin and its stand;
The garments for service, the holy garments for Aaron the priest, and the garments for his sons to serve me as priests.
and the anointing oil and the fragrant incense for the sanctuary. They shall make everything I have commanded you.”
The Lord said to Moses,
Tell the Israelites, “You must observe the Sabbaths, because this is a sign between me and you throughout your generations, so that you may know that I am the Lord who makes you holy.”
Keep the Sabbath, because it is holy to you. Whoever profanes it must certainly be put to death. Whoever does work on it must be cut off from his people.
You shall work for six days, but on the seventh day there is a Sabbath of rest, holy to the Lord. Whoever does work on the Sabbath day must certainly be put to death.
The Israelites shall observe the Sabbath to the Lord, keeping the Sabbath throughout their generations as an everlasting covenant.
It is a sign forever between me and the house of Israel, because in six days the Lord made heaven and earth, the seas and everything in them, and on the seventh day he stopped and rested.
When he finished speaking with Moses on Mount Sinai, he gave him the two tablets of the testimony, stone tablets inscribed by the finger of God.

The people saw that Moses was taking a long time to come down from the mountain. They gathered around Aaron and said to him, “Come, make us gods who will go before us. As for this man Moses, who brought us up from the land of Egypt, we do not know what has happened to him.”
Aaron said to them, “Take off the gold earrings in the ears of your wives, your sons, and your daughters, and bring them to me.”
All the people took off the earrings that were in their ears and brought them to Aaron.
He took the gold from them, shaped it in a mold, and made it into a cast calf. They said, “This is your god, Israel, who brought you up from the land of Egypt.”
Aaron was afraid and built an altar before it. Then Aaron proclaimed, “Tomorrow is a festival to the Lord.”
They rose early the next day, offered burnt offerings, sacrificed fellowship offerings, and brought offerings. The people sat down to eat and drink, and got up to laugh and play.
The Lord said to Moses, “Go down! Leave this place, because your people, whom you brought out of Egypt, have become corrupt.

They have quickly turned aside from the way I commanded them. They have made themselves a cast calf, bowed down to it, sacrificed to it, and said, “This is your god, Israel, who brought you up from the land of Egypt.”
The Lord said to Moses, “I have seen this people, and look, they are a stubborn people.”
“Now leave me alone, so that my anger may burn against them and I may destroy them. I will make you into a great nation.”
Moses prayed before the Lord his God and said, “No, Lord! Do not let your anger grow fierce against your people, whom you brought out of Egypt with your great power and your uplifted arm.”

Do not let the Egyptians say, “He brought them out to harm them, to kill them among the mountains and wipe them off the face of the earth.” Turn away from your fierce anger, and relent from bringing disaster on your people.

Remember Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, your servants, to whom you swore by yourself and said, “I will make your descendants as numerous as the stars in heaven. I will give your descendants all the land I promised, and they will inherit it forever.”
The Lord relented concerning the disaster he had said he would bring upon his people.
Moses turned and came down from the mountain with the two tablets of the testimony in his hand. The tablets were inscribed on both sides; they were inscribed on this side and that.
The tablets were God's work, and the writing was God's writing, engraved on the tablets.
Joshua heard the sound of the people fighting and said to Moses, “There is the sound of battle in the camp.”
Moses said to him, “It is not the sound of mighty warriors speaking, nor the sound of the weak. Rather, it is the sound of sin that I hear.”
When he approached the camp, he saw the calf and the cymbals. Moses became furious, threw the tablets from his hand, and broke them at the foot of the mountain.

He took the calf they had made and burned it in the fire. He ground it with a file until it was as fine as dust, scattered its powder over the surface of the water, and made the house of Israel drink it.
Moses said to Aaron, “What did these people do to you, that you brought such a great sin upon them?”
Aaron said, “Do not let my lord’s anger burn. You know that these people are evil.”
They said to me, “Make us gods who will go before us. As for this Moses, who brought us up from the land of Egypt, we do not know what has happened to him.”
I said to them, ‘Whoever has gold, bring it to me.’ They brought it to me, and I threw it into the fire, and this calf came out.
Moses saw that the people had sinned, because Aaron had led them into sin, giving them a bad name among their descendants.
Moses stood at the entrance of the tent and said, ‘Whoever is on the Lord’s side, come to me.’ All the descendants of Levi gathered around him.

Moses said to them, ‘This is what the Lord, the God of Israel, says: Each of you, strap your sword to your side. Go back and forth through the camp, from entrance to entrance, and each of you kill your brother, your companion, and your relative.’
The descendants of Levi did as Moses had said, and about three thousand men from among the people fell that day.
Moses said to them, ‘Consecrate yourselves to the Lord today, each at the cost of his son and his brother, so that a blessing may come upon you today.’
The next day Moses said to the people, ‘You have committed this great sin. Now I will go up to the Lord; perhaps he will forgive your sins.’
Moses returned to the Lord and said, ‘I beg you, Lord God! These people have indeed committed a great sin and made gods of gold for themselves.’
“Now, if you will forgive their sins—but if not, blot me out of your book that you have written.”
The Lord said to Moses, “Whoever has sinned against me, I will blot out of my book.”
‘Now go, lead these people to the place I tell you. Look, my angel will go ahead of you. But on the day when I call them to account, I will punish them for their sins.’
The Lord struck the people because they had worshiped the calf that Aaron made.

The Lord said to Moses, ‘Leave this place and go up, you and your people whom you brought out of Egypt, to the land that I swore to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, telling them, “I will give it to your descendants.”’
‘I will send an angel ahead of you, and he will destroy the Canaanites, Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.’
‘Go to a land flowing with milk and honey. But I will not go up among you, because you are a stubborn people, lest I destroy you on the way.’
When the people heard this bad news, they mourned, and no one put on his armor.

The Lord said to Moses, ‘Tell the Israelites: You are a stubborn people. If I went up among you for even one moment, I would destroy you. Now take off your ornaments, and I will decide what to do with you.’
So the Israelites took off their armor from Mount Horeb onward.
Moses took his tent and pitched it outside the camp, far away from the camp, and called it the Tent of Meeting. Everyone who sought the Lord would go out to the Tent of Meeting outside the camp.
Whenever Moses went out to the tent, all the people would rise and stand, each at the entrance of his own tent, and watch Moses until he entered the tent.
Whenever Moses entered the tent, the pillar of cloud would come down and stand at the entrance of the tent, and he would speak with Moses.
All the people would see the pillar of cloud standing at the entrance of the tent, and all the people would rise and bow down, each at the entrance of his own tent.
The Lord spoke with Moses face to face, as a man speaks with his companion. Then Moses would return to the camp, but his attendant, the young man Hoshea son of Nun, would not leave the tent.

Moses said to the Lord, ‘Look, you have told me, “Lead these people up,” but you have not shown me whom you will send with me. Yet you have said, “I know you by name, and you have also found favor in my sight.”’
‘Now, if I have found favor in your sight, show me your way so that I may know you and find favor in your sight. And consider that this great nation is your people.’
The Lord said to Moses, “Go before me, and I will give you rest.”
He said to him, “If you do not go with us, do not bring us up from here.”
‘How will it be known here that I and your people have found favor in your sight, unless you go with us? Then I and your people will be distinguished from all the peoples on the face of the earth.’
The Lord said to Moses, ‘I will do just what you have said, because you have found favor in my sight, and I know you by name.’
He said, “Show me your glory.”

He said, ‘I will make all my goodness pass before you, and I will proclaim the name of the Lord before you. I will show favor to whomever I show favor, and I will have mercy on whomever I have mercy.’
He said, “You cannot see my face, because no human can see me and live.”
The Lord said to Moses, “Here is a place beside me. Stand on the rock.”
“When my glory passes by, I will put you in a hollow in the rock and cover you with my hand until I have passed by.”
Then I will take my hand away, and you will see my back, but my face will not be seen.
The Lord said to Moses, ‘Cut out two stone tablets for yourself like the first ones, and I will write on the tablets the words that were on the first tablets, which you broke.’
Be ready in the morning, and go up Mount Sinai in the morning. Stand there on the mountaintop.
‘No one is to go up with you, and no one is to be seen anywhere on the mountain. Not even sheep or cattle are to graze in front of that mountain.’
He cut two stone tablets like the first ones. Moses rose early in the morning and went up Mount Sinai, as the Lord had commanded him, taking the two stone tablets in his hand.
The Lord came down in a cloud and stood with him there, and proclaimed the name of the Lord.
The Lord passed before him and proclaimed, “The Lord, the Lord, a merciful and compassionate God, slow to anger and abundant in goodness and faithfulness,

preserving goodness for thousands of generations, forgiving sins and offenses, but certainly not acquitting the guilty, bringing the consequences of the fathers’ offenses upon their children and grandchildren, to the third and fourth generations.”
Moses hurried, fell to the ground, and worshiped.
He said, “If I have found favor in your eyes, my Lord, let my Lord now go among us, for they are a stubborn people. Forgive our offenses and our sins, and take us as your inheritance.”

He said, “Look, I am establishing a covenant before all your people. I will perform wonders that have never been done anywhere on earth or among any of the nations. All these people among whom you live will see the work of the Lord, for what I am doing with you is awe-inspiring.
Observe what I command you today. Look, I am destroying before you the Canaanites, Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.
Be careful not to make a covenant with the inhabitants of the land to which you are going, so that they do not become a snare to you.
Tear down their altars, smash their sacred pillars, and cut down their idols.
Do not worship another god, because the Lord, whose name is Jealous, is a jealous God.
Do not make a covenant with the inhabitants of the land, lest they stray after the objects of their worship and sacrifice to their gods, and invite you, and you eat from their sacrifices.
You might take their daughters for your sons and give your daughters to their sons, and your daughters might stray after their gods and lead your sons astray after their gods.
Do not make gods of cast metal for yourself.

Observe the Festival of Unleavened Bread. For seven days you shall eat unleavened bread, as I commanded you, at the appointed time in the month of blossoms, because in the month of blossoms you came out of Egypt.
Every firstborn that opens the womb belongs to me, including all the firstborn of your livestock, both cattle and sheep.
Redeem the firstborn of livestock with a lamb. If you do not redeem it, kill it. Redeem every firstborn among your sons. You shall not appear before me empty-handed.
Work for six days, but rest on the seventh day. Rest even during sowing and harvest.
Celebrate the Festival of Weeks at the beginning of the wheat harvest, and the Festival of Ingathering at the end of the year.
Three times a year all your males are to appear before the Lord, the God of Israel.
For I will destroy nations before you and enlarge your territory. No one will covet your land when you go up to appear before the Lord your God three times a year.
Do not offer the blood of a sacrifice together with leavened bread, and do not let the sacrifice of the Passover festival remain overnight until morning.
Bring the first of your land’s produce to the house of the Lord your God. Do not cook a young goat in its mother’s milk.
The Lord said to Moses, “Write down these words, because on the basis of these words I have established a covenant with you and with all Israel.”
He was there with the Lord forty days and forty nights. He ate no bread and drank no water. He wrote on the stone tablets the words of the covenant, the Ten Commandments.

When Moses came down from Mount Sinai, the two tablets of the testimony were in Moses’ hand as he came down from the mountain. Moses did not know that the skin of his face had become radiant when God spoke with him.
Aaron and all Israel saw that the skin of Moses’ face had become radiant, and they were afraid to approach him.
Moses called them, and Aaron and all the leaders of the assembly came to him. Moses spoke with them.
Then all the Israelites approached him, and he commanded them everything that the Lord had spoken to him on Mount Sinai.
When Moses finished speaking with them, he put a veil over his face.
Whenever Moses went in before the Lord to speak with him, he would remove the veil until he came out. Then he would come out and tell the people of Israel what he had been commanded.
The Israelites would see Moses’ face, that the skin of Moses’ face had become radiant. Moses would remove the veil from his face whenever he went in to speak with him.
Moses gathered the whole assembly of the Israelites and said to them, “These are the things that the Lord has commanded you to do.
For six days you shall work, but the seventh day shall be holy, a Sabbath of rest to the Lord. Whoever does any work on it shall be put to death.
Do not light a fire in any of your dwellings on the Sabbath day.”
Moses said to the whole congregation of the Israelites, “This is what the Lord has commanded you to do:
Take from among yourselves a contribution for the Lord. Everyone who has resolved in his heart shall bring a contribution to the Lord: gold, silver, and bronze.
blue and purple material, scarlet dye, spun linen, and goats’ hair;
rams’ skins dyed red, blue skins, and boxwood;
oil for lighting, and spices for the anointing oil and for the fragrant incense;
beryl stones and stones for setting in the ephod and the breastpiece.
Let all the skilled people among you come and make everything that the Lord has commanded:
the tabernacle, its tent and its covering, its clasps, its boards, its bars, its pillars, and its bases;
the ark and its carrying poles, the atonement cover, and the curtain for the entrance;
the table and its carrying poles, all its utensils, and the bread of the Presence;
the lampstand for lighting, its utensils and its lamps, and the oil for lighting;
The incense altar and its poles, the anointing oil and the fragrant incense, and the curtain for the entrance of the tabernacle;
the altar of burnt offering and its bronze grating, its poles and all its utensils, and the basin and its stand.
And the hangings of the courtyard, its pillars and their bases, and the curtain for the courtyard entrance.
And the pegs of the tabernacle, the pegs of the courtyard, and their ropes.
And the garments for service in the sanctuary, the holy garments for Aaron the priest, and the garments for his sons to serve as priests.
Then the whole congregation of the Israelites left Moses' presence.
Everyone whose heart moved him and everyone whose spirit prompted him brought an offering to the Lord for the work on the tent of meeting, for all its service, and for the holy garments.

The men came bringing offerings along with the women. Everyone whose heart moved them brought bracelets, earrings, rings, necklaces, and all kinds of gold objects—everyone who set apart an offering of gold for the Lord.
Everyone who had blue, purple, or scarlet yarn, fine linen, goats’ hair, rams’ skins dyed red, or blue-dyed skins brought them.
Everyone who set apart an offering of silver or bronze brought the offering to the Lord. Everyone who had boxwood for any of the work of the service brought it.
Every skilled woman spun with her own hands. They brought what they had spun: blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and fine linen.
All the women whose hearts moved them to use their skill spun the hair.
The leaders brought beryl stones and stones for setting in the ephod and the breastpiece,
and spices and oil for lighting, for the anointing oil, and for the fragrant incense.
Every man and woman whose heart moved them to bring something for all the work that the Lord had commanded through Moses brought it. The Israelites brought an offering to the Lord.
Moses said to the Israelites, “See, the Lord has called by name Bezalel son of Uri, son of Hur, from the tribe of Judah.”
He has filled him with the Spirit of God, with wisdom, understanding, knowledge, and skill in every kind of work,
to devise designs and to work in gold, silver, and bronze,
in cutting stones for setting, and in woodworking, to perform every kind of skilled work.
He has also given him the ability to teach—both him and Oholiab son of Ahisamach, from the tribe of Dan.
He filled them with skill to do every kind of work as carpenters, craftsmen, embroiderers in blue, purple, fine linen, and scarlet, and weavers—workers in every craft and makers of designs.

Bezalel, Oholiab, and every skilled man in whom the Lord had placed wisdom and understanding carried out all the work for the service of the sanctuary, knowing how to do it according to everything the Lord had commanded.
Moses called Bezalel and Oholiab, and every skilled man in whose heart the Lord had placed wisdom—everyone whose heart moved him to come forward to do the work.
They received from Moses all the offerings that the Israelites had brought for carrying out the work on the tent of meeting. The people continued bringing him offerings morning after morning.
They brought all the skilled workers who were doing the work of the sanctuary, each from the work they were doing.
They said to Moses, "The people are bringing more than is needed for the work that the Lord commanded us to do."
Moses gave an order, and heralds proclaimed throughout the camp, “No man or woman is to do any more work for the offering for the sanctuary.” So the people were stopped from bringing anything more.
The materials were sufficient for all the work that had to be done, and they had some left over.
All the skilled workers made the tabernacle with ten curtains of finely spun linen and blue, purple, and scarlet yarn. They made them with cherubim worked into them by a craftsman.
Each curtain was twenty-eight cubits long and four cubits wide. All the curtains had the same measurements.
They joined five curtains together, and they joined the other five curtains to one another.
They made loops of blue yarn along the edge of one curtain at the end of the joined set. They did the same along the edge of the curtain at the end of the other joined set.
They made fifty loops on one curtain, and they made fifty loops along the edge of the curtain in the other joined set. The loops were opposite one another.
They made fifty gold clasps and joined the curtains to one another with the clasps, so that the tabernacle became one whole.
They made haircloth curtains to spread over the tabernacle. They made eleven curtains.
Each curtain was thirty cubits long and four cubits wide. All eleven curtains had the same measurements.
They joined five curtains together, and the other six curtains together.
They made loops: fifty loops along the edge of the curtain at the end of the joined set, and fifty loops along the edge of the curtain in the other joined set.
They made fifty bronze clasps to join the tabernacle together so that it would be one whole.
They made a covering for the tabernacle from rams’ skins dyed red, and an outer covering of blue-dyed skins above it.
They made upright boards of boxwood for the tabernacle.
Each board was ten cubits long and a cubit and a half wide.
There were two tenons on one board, and two tenons on another board, aligned opposite one another. They made all the boards of the tabernacle this way.
They made the boards for the tabernacle: twenty boards for the south side.
They made forty silver bases beneath the twenty boards: two bases beneath one board for its two tenons, and two bases beneath another board for its two tenons.
For the other side of the tabernacle, the north side, they made twenty boards.
And forty silver bases: two bases beneath one board, and two bases beneath another board.
For the rear of the tabernacle, on the west, they made six boards.
They made two boards for the corner of the tabernacle at the rear.
They were paired at the bottom, and their tops were joined together at a single ring. They did this for both of them, at the two corners.
There were eight boards, with sixteen silver bases: two bases beneath one board and two bases beneath another board.
They made crossbars of boxwood: five for the boards on one side of the tabernacle.
And five crossbars for the boards on the other side of the tabernacle, and five crossbars for the boards at the rear of the tabernacle, on the west.
They made the middle crossbar to pass through the middle of the boards from one end to the other.
They overlaid the boards with gold and made their rings of gold as holders for the crossbars. They also overlaid the crossbars with gold.
They made a curtain of blue, purple, scarlet-dyed yarn, and finely spun linen. He made it with cherubim, the work of a skilled craftsman.
They made four pillars of boxwood for it and overlaid them with gold. Their capitals were gold, and they made four silver bases for them.
They made a curtain for the entrance of the tabernacle, of blue, purple, scarlet-dyed yarn, and finely spun linen, worked with embroidery.
Its pillars were five, and their capitals were five. The covering of their tops and their overlay were gold, and their five bases were bronze.
Bezalel made the ark of boxwood, two and a half cubits long, a cubit and a half wide, and a cubit and a half high.
He overlaid it with pure gold, inside and out, and made a gold molding around it.
He cast four gold rings for it at its four corners: two rings on one side and two rings on the other side.
He made poles of boxwood and overlaid them with gold.
He inserted the poles into the rings on the sides of the ark to carry the ark.
He made the atonement cover of pure gold, two and a half cubits long and a cubit and a half wide.
He made two cherubim of gold. He made them of cast work at the two ends of the atonement cover.
One cherub was on this side, and another cherub on the other side. He made the cherubim above the atonement cover, on its two sides.
The cherubim spread their wings upward, sheltering the atonement cover with their wings. Their faces were toward one another; the faces of the cherubim were turned toward the atonement cover.
He made the table of boxwood, two cubits long, one cubit wide, and a cubit and a half high.
He overlaid it with pure gold and made a gold molding all around its rim.
He made a rim a handbreadth wide around it, and made a gold molding around its rim.
He cast four gold rings for it and placed the rings at its four corners, on its four legs.
Its rings were alongside its rim, as holders for the poles used to carry the table.
He made the poles of boxwood and overlaid them with gold, to carry the table with them.
He made the utensils for the table—its dishes, its spoons, its pitchers, and the vessels used for pouring drink offerings—of pure gold.
He made the lampstand of pure gold. He made the lampstand as cast work; its base, its branches, its cups, its knobs, and its flowers were all part of it.
Six branches extended from its sides: three branches of the lampstand from one side, and three branches of the lampstand from the other side.
Three cups were set on one branch, with knobs and flowers, and three cups were set on another branch, with knobs and flowers. It was the same for all six branches extending from the lampstand.
On the lampstand itself, four cups were set, with knobs and lilies.

There was a knob beneath two branches extending from it, a knob beneath two branches extending from it, and a knob beneath two branches extending from it. It was the same for all six branches extending from the lampstand.
Its knobs and branches were part of it. The whole thing was a single casting of pure gold.
He made its seven lamps, its wick trimmers, and its trays of pure gold.
He made it and all its utensils from a talent of pure gold.
He made the incense altar of boxwood, one cubit long and one cubit wide, square, and two cubits high. Its horns were part of it.
He overlaid it with pure gold—its top, its sides all around, and its horns. He made a gold molding around it.
He made two gold rings for it beneath its molding, at its two corners, on its two sides, as holders for the poles used to carry it.
He made the poles of boxwood and overlaid them with gold.
He made the holy anointing oil and the incense of pure spices, the work of a perfumer.
He made the altar of burnt offering of boxwood, five cubits long and five cubits wide, square, and three cubits high.
He made its horns on its four corners. Its horns were part of it, and he overlaid it with bronze.
He made all the altar's utensils: the pots, shovels, basins, strainers, meat forks, and firepans. He made all its utensils of bronze.
He made a grating for the altar, a bronze network beneath its rim, extending from below halfway up.
He cast four rings for it at the four corners of the bronze base, as holders for the poles.
He made the poles of boxwood and overlaid them with bronze.
He inserted the poles into the rings on the sides of the altar to carry it with them. He made it hollow, out of boards.
He made the bronze basin and its bronze stand from the mirrors of the women who came to pray at the entrance to the tent of meeting.
He made the courtyard. On the south side, the courtyard hangings were of finely twisted linen, a hundred cubits long.
Their pillars numbered twenty, and their bronze bases numbered twenty. The capitals of the pillars and their covering were silver.
On the north side there were one hundred cubits, with twenty pillars and twenty bronze bases. The capitals of the pillars and their covering were silver.
On the west side the hangings measured fifty cubits, with ten pillars and ten bases. The capitals of the pillars and their covering were silver.
On the east side, the length was fifty cubits.
The hangings on one side were fifteen cubits long, with three pillars and three bases.
On the other side, on either side of the courtyard entrance, the hangings measured fifteen cubits on each side, with three pillars and three bases.
All the hangings around the courtyard were of finely twisted linen.

The bases for the pillars were bronze, and the capitals of the pillars and their covering were silver. The covering of their tops was silver, and all the pillars of the courtyard were overlaid with silver.

The curtain for the courtyard entrance was embroidered work, made of blue, purple, scarlet yarn, and finely spun linen. Its length was twenty cubits, and its height and width were five cubits, matching the courtyard hangings.
There were four pillars and four bronze bases. Their capitals were silver, and the covering of their tops and their overlay were silver.
All the pegs of the tabernacle and of the courtyard all around were bronze.
These are the accounts of the tabernacle, the tabernacle of the testimony, recorded at Moses’ command through the work of the Levites under the direction of Ithamar, son of Aaron the priest.
Bezalel son of Uri, son of Hur, from the tribe of Judah, made everything that the Lord commanded Moses.
With him was Oholiab son of Ahisamach, from the tribe of Dan, a carpenter, craftsman, and embroiderer in blue, purple, scarlet yarn, and linen.
All the gold used for the work, for all the work of the sanctuary—the gold of the offering—amounted to twenty-nine talents and four hundred thirty shekels, by the sanctuary standard.
The silver from those counted in the congregation amounted to one hundred talents and one thousand seven hundred seventy-five shekels, by the sanctuary standard.
The weight per person was half a shekel, by the sanctuary standard, for everyone who passed through the census, from twenty years old and upward: six hundred three thousand five hundred fifty people.
The one hundred talents of silver were used to cast the bases of the sanctuary and the bases of the curtain: one hundred bases from one hundred talents, one talent for each base.
With the one thousand seven hundred seventy-five, he made capitals for the pillars and a covering for their tops, and overlaid them with silver.
All the bronze contributed as an offering was seventy talents and two thousand four hundred shekels.
With it he made the bases for the entrance to the tent of meeting, the bronze altar and its bronze grating, and all the altar’s utensils.
He also made the bases all around the courtyard, the bases for the courtyard entrance, all the tent pegs of the tabernacle, and all the pegs around the courtyard.
From blue, purple, and scarlet yarn they made garments for service in the sanctuary. They also made the sacred garments for Aaron, as the Lord commanded Moses.
They made the ephod of gold, blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and finely spun linen.
They hammered out sheets of gold and cut them into threads to work into the blue, purple, scarlet yarn, and linen, the work of a skilled craftsman.
They made shoulder pieces for it, attached at its two sides to join it together.
The waistband of the ephod was made as one piece with it, of the same workmanship: gold, blue, purple, scarlet yarn, and finely spun linen, as the Lord commanded Moses.
They prepared beryl stones, mounted and set in gold, engraved like a seal with the names of the sons of Israel.
They placed them on the shoulder pieces of the ephod as memorial stones for the sons of Israel, as the Lord commanded Moses.
They made the breastpiece with skilled craftsmanship, like the workmanship of the ephod, from gold, blue and purple yarn, scarlet thread, and finely spun linen.
It was square and folded double. They made the breastpiece a span long and a span wide when folded double.
They set four rows of stones in it. The first row was a ruby, a topaz, and an emerald—one row.
The next row was a carbuncle, a sapphire, and a diamond.
The third row was a jacinth, an agate, and an amethyst.
The fourth row: chrysolite, beryl, and jasper. They were enclosed and set entirely in gold.
The stones bore the names of the sons of Israel, twelve according to their names, engraved like the engravings of a seal, each with its own name, for the twelve tribes.
They made paired chains for the breastpiece, braided work of pure gold.
They made two gold settings and two gold rings, and they put the two rings on the two sides of the breastpiece.
They attached the two braided gold chains to the two rings on the two sides of the breastpiece.
They attached the two braided chains on the two sides to the two settings, and they attached them to the shoulder pieces of the ephod, at its front.
They made two gold rings and placed them on the two sides of the breastpiece, on its inner edge facing the ephod.
They made two gold rings and attached them to the two shoulder pieces of the ephod on the inside, facing its front, near its joining, above the ephod’s waistband.

They fastened the breastpiece by its rings to the rings of the ephod with a blue cord, so that it would lie above the ephod’s waistband and the breastpiece would not come loose from the ephod, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
They made the robe of the ephod entirely of blue woven fabric.
The opening of the robe was in its center, like the opening of a coat of mail, with a border around its opening so that it would not tear.
They made pomegranates along the hem of the robe from blue and purple yarn, scarlet thread, and finely spun linen.
They made bells of pure gold and fastened the bells among the pomegranates, all around the hem of the robe, among the pomegranates.
There were gold bells and pomegranates all around the hem of the robe for service, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
They made woven tunics of fine linen for Aaron and his sons.
And the linen turban, the splendid linen caps, and the undergarment of finely spun linen.
And the sash was of finely spun linen, blue and purple yarn, scarlet thread, and finely spun linen, the work of an embroiderer, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
They made the crown of holy consecration from pure gold and wrote an inscription on it, engraved like a seal: “Holy to the Lord.”
They attached a blue cord to it so that it would be on the upper part of the turban, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
All the work of the tent of meeting was completed. The Israelites did everything that the Lord had commanded Moses; that is what they did.
They brought the tabernacle to Moses: the tent and all its equipment, its rings, its clasps, its boards, its pegs, its crossbars, its pillars, and its bases.
And the covering of rams’ skins dyed scarlet, the covering of rams’ skins dyed blue, and the curtain screening the entrance.
And the ark of the testimony with its carrying poles and the atonement cover.
And the table with all its utensils and the bread of the Presence.
And the pure lampstand and its lamps, the lamps arranged in its rows and all its utensils, and the oil for lighting.
And the gold altar, the anointing oil, the fragrant incense, and the curtain for the entrance to the tabernacle.
And the bronze altar, its bronze grating, its carrying poles and all its utensils, and the basin and its stand.
And the hangings of the courtyard, its pillars and its bases, the curtain for the courtyard entrance, its ropes and its pegs, and all the equipment for the service of the tent of meeting.
And the garments for ministering in the sanctuary, the holy garments for Aaron the priest, and the garments for his sons to serve as priests.
Just as the Lord commanded Moses, so the Israelites did all the work.
Moses inspected all the work, and there it was: they had done it as the Lord had commanded Moses. That is what they had done, and Moses blessed them.
The Lord said to Moses:
On the first day of the first month, set up the tent of meeting.
Place the ark of the testimony there, and spread the curtain to screen the ark.
Bring in the table and arrange the bread in rows. Bring in the lampstand and light its lamps.
Set the gold altar for incense before the ark of the testimony, and hang the curtain at the entrance of the tabernacle.
Place the altar of burnt offering before the entrance to the tent of meeting.
Place the basin between the tent of meeting and the altar, and put water in it.
Set up the courtyard all around, and hang the curtain at the entrance to the courtyard.
Take the anointing oil and anoint the tabernacle and everything in it. Consecrate it and all its utensils, and it will be holy.
Anoint the altar of burnt offering and all its utensils. Consecrate the altar, and the altar will be most holy.
Anoint the basin and its stand, and consecrate them.
Bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance to the tent of meeting, and wash them with water.
Dress Aaron in the sacred garments, anoint him, and consecrate him so that he may serve me as priest.
Bring his sons forward and dress them in tunics.
Anoint them as you anointed your brother Aaron, so that they may serve me as priests. Their anointing will give them a priesthood forever, throughout their generations.
Moses did everything the Lord commanded him; that is what he did.
On the first day of the first month in the second year, on the first day of the week, the tabernacle was set up.
Moses set up the tabernacle. He drove in its pegs, put its boards in place, fastened its bars, and set up its pillars.
He spread a covering over the tabernacle and laid the tabernacle's covering over it on top, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
He took the testimony and placed it in the ark. He put the poles on the ark and placed the atonement cover on top of the ark.
He brought the ark into the tabernacle, took the entrance curtain, and spread it over the ark of the testimony, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
He placed the table in the tent of meeting, along the north side of the tabernacle, outside the curtain.
He arranged the bread on it in rows before the LORD, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
He placed the lampstand in the tent of meeting opposite the table, along the south side of the tabernacle.
He lit its lamps before the LORD, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
He placed the gold altar in the tent of meeting before the curtain.
He burned fragrant incense on it, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
He put up the curtain at the entrance to the tabernacle.
He placed the altar of burnt offering at the entrance to the tent of meeting and offered a burnt offering and fine flour on it, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
He placed the basin between the tent of meeting and the altar and put water in it for washing.
Moses, Aaron, and Aaron’s sons washed their hands and feet with water from it.
Whenever they entered the tent of meeting or approached the altar, they washed, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
He set up the courtyard all around the tabernacle and the altar, and put the curtain at the entrance to the courtyard. So Moses finished the work.
The cloud covered the tent of meeting, and the glory of the Lord filled the tabernacle.
Moses could not enter the tent of meeting because the cloud had settled over it, and the glory of the Lord filled the tabernacle.
Whenever the cloud rose from above the tabernacle, the Israelites set out on all their journeys.
But if the cloud did not rise, they did not set out until the day it rose.
For the Lord's cloud was over the tabernacle by day, and fire was in it by night, in the sight of the whole house of Israel throughout all their journeys.
